Governorship Election Presidential Gubernatorial 2027 Grammys: Six Nigerian stars earn nominations as five new categories debut (FULL LIST) The artistes secured nominations across the African, global music and R&B categories ahead of the February ceremony. by Ozaveshe Precious November 16, 2026 Reading Time: 6 mins read 0 Add us on Google Six Nigerian music stars have earned nominations for the 69th Annual Grammy Awards, scheduled for 7 February 2027 in Los Angeles, United States.
The Recording Academy announced the nominees on Monday, with Davido, Tems, Asake, Ayra Starr, Wizkid and Burna Boy recognised across four categories.
Nigerian artistes secured three of the five nominations for Best Global Music Album and featured on four of the five songs competing for Best African Music Performance.
Davido earned a nomination for Oriadé, which will compete for Best Global Music Album.
Tems was nominated in the same category for Love Is a Kingdom, while Ayra Starr secured a place with Starrgirl.
The Nigerian albums will compete against EQUILIBRIVM by Brazilian singer Anitta and Hope!! by Beninese music star Angélique Kidjo.
The nomination marks another Grammy recognition for Davido, who previously received three nominations at the 2024 awards but did not win.

Nigerian artistes featured prominently in the Best African Music Performance category.
Asake earned a nomination for Gratitude, while his collaboration with Wizkid, Jogodo, also made the list.
Tems was nominated for Big Daddy, while Ayra Starr received recognition for Aye Kan (Are You Coming Back?), her collaboration with Ms Kidjo.
The only nominated entry without a Nigerian artiste is No Tradition, No Africa by Ghanaian musicians King Ayisoba and Rocky Dawuni.
The Recording Academy confirmed the nominees in a video published on its official Instagram page on Monday.
Tems also earned a Best R&B Song nomination for What You Need, taking her total nominations for the 2027 awards to three.
She will compete against Let Me by Victoria Monét, My Muse by Leon Thomas, Out The Window by Kehlani and Pressha by Jill Scott.
Tems has previously won two Grammy Awards. She received Best Melodic Rap Performance in 2023 for her contribution to Future’s Wait For U, featuring Drake, and won Best African Music Performance in 2025 for Love Me JeJe. The Recording Academy lists her with two wins and eight nominations before the latest cycle.
Burna Boy earned a Best Global Music Performance nomination for Dai Dai, his collaboration with Colombian singer Shakira.
The song will compete against Varuvaaiy by Devan Ekambaram featuring Susha; Una Flor En Cada Estrella by KerreKe, Mireya and Alex E. Chávez; Bando [Orchestral] by Angélique Kidjo featuring Pharrell Williams and Quavo; and Porcelana by Rosalía and Dougie F.
The nomination extends Burna Boy’s Grammy record. He won Best Global Music Album in 2021 for Twice As Tall.
The 69th Annual Grammy Awards will take place at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles on 7 February 2027.
The ceremony will air live on ABC and stream on Disney+ and Hulu.
The eligibility period covered recordings released between 31 August 2025 and 28 August 2026. Final-round voting will run from 10 December 2026 to 7 January 2027.
Five new categories will debut at the ceremony: Best Asian Pop Music Performance, Best R&B Collaboration or Duo/Group Performance, Best Traditional Pop Vocal Performance, Best Traditional Folk Album and Best Latin Song.
* Aye Kan (Are You Coming Back?) — Angélique Kidjo and Ayra Starr
* No Tradition, No Africa — King Ayisoba featuring Rocky Dawuni
-“Aye Kan (Are You Coming Back?)” — Angélique Kidjo & Ayra Starr
-“No Tradition, No Africa” — King Ayisoba featuring Rocky Dawuni
-“Una Flor En Cada Estrella” — KerreKe, Mireya & Alex E. Chávez
-“Bando [Orchestral]” — Angélique Kidjo featuring Pharrell Williams & Quavo
– you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love – Olivia Rodrigo
– ‘House’ [From Wuthering Heights] – John Cale and Charli XCX
– ‘No Place Like Home’ [From Wicked: For Good] – Cynthia Erivo
– ‘RUNWAY’ [From The Devil Wears Prada 2] – Lady Gaga and Doechii
– ‘Hasta Jesús Tuvo un Mal Día’ – CA7RIEL and Paco Amoroso, featuring Sting
– ‘The Life of a Showgirl’ – Taylor Swift and Sabrina Carpenter
– Bates: The Amazing Adventures Of Kavalier & Clay – Mason Bates
– Akiho: Beneath Lighted Coffers & Concerto For Steel Pans & Orchestra – Andy Akiho
– Bridgetower Project – Beethoven, Florence Price, Paquito D’Rivera – Ilya Kaler and Rasa Vitauskaite
– Kouyoumdjian: Paper Pianos – Alan Pierson and Alarm Will Sound
– Puts: Emily – No Prisoner Be – Joyce DiDonato and Time For Three
– ‘all that’s left’ – Nicole Zuraitis featuring Gilad Hekselman
The categories above reflect the nomination information contained in the supplied updates. The Recording Academy’s complete list covers 100 categories.
